title: C313 — Inline connector reference
introduction:
I use this reference like a connector seating chart: the drawing locates a cavity, and the matching table explains its electrical job. Start with the connector identity, then check the face gender and harness heading before reading the diagram and circuit rows together.

In the male drawing, the A cavities occupy the upper section and the B cavities occupy the lower section. Read the individual labels—the lower section does not simply repeat the upper section’s numbering direction. The housing outline provides visual landmarks, but its projections are not identified as release mechanisms. Shaded cavities have no supplied legend, so shading alone is not an electrical verdict.

Match a cavity to its circuit number, then read its color, function, qualifier and terminal information across the same row. Repeated cavities can have different entries; keep those distinctions instead of choosing whichever looks familiar. Functions identified as fuse-or-circuit-breaker supplies retain both protection alternatives.

This is an identification and circuit-reading reference. Physical viewing direction, the gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used codes are not established here. It does not teach connector access, probing, wire selection or pigtail installation.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the cavity count shown in the drawings. Each face has its own assignment table; do not transfer a qualifier or function from one face to fill a gap in the other. Count and overlapping assignment applicability remain unresolved, including impact-sensor alternatives. This reference does not establish a physical wiring configuration.

edits.why: I keep the face drawing paired with its harness identification and adjacent parts table. Gender identifies this face; it does not establish whether a physical connector is being viewed from the terminal side or wire side.

Use the cavity label to join the drawing to the table, then read across the complete row. Circuit identity and function distinguish the connections; color alone cannot resolve repeated entries. Blank qualifiers do not explain which configuration applies.

This section identifies the female face separately. Its upper A group and lower B group use their own printed positions, arranged differently from the male drawing. Match each complete label to this face’s table rather than assuming the same displayed position across faces. The outlines are drawing landmarks, not a release method or a statement of physical viewing direction.

Read each complete row with its own qualifier and terminal entry. A right-hand-drive qualifier on a female row does not supply missing applicability for a male alternative. Unqualified overlapping entries remain unresolved. The two faces also contain different turn-signal, lamp-color, lock, mirror and speaker assignments at corresponding labels. Those records do not establish a matched physical configuration; do not transfer or combine them. Named ground, antenna negative, speaker negative and impact-sensor connections retain their distinct labels; no probing or restraint-service procedure is supplied.

The two catalog rows list different service parts and gauge entries against the same engineering-shell designation. Keep each row intact. Neither the shared shell nor these listings establishes interchangeability, which kit fits a particular vehicle, or a terminal repair method.

originalAuthorHold: The same cavities have unqualified driver-side and passenger-side assignments: A14 lists VR217 and VR218, while A15 lists RR131 and RR132. Both entries remain unchanged; the applicable assignment cannot be selected from this evidence.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 145 primary units, seven complete pages/two figures and five edits. Original first CLI author covered 55 units/two headings. Introduction explicitly discloses count disagreement and cross-face assignment limitations; female face and pigtail headings complete the partial draft. Original two edits remain unchanged. Original partial author remains separate; physical count and unqualified gauge/terminal alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
